name: AZ-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Stanton holds a roughly four-to-one fundraising and cash advantage over Jasser
The district leans Democratic (D+4) and the national environment favors Democrats
Polymarket prices a Stanton win at about 97 percent
No outside spending opposes Stanton and no public general-election polling exists
model.rationale: Stanton's large financial edge, the district's Democratic lean, and a favorable national environment point to a comfortable incumbent win, and prediction markets corroborate that view despite the absence of polling.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a sharper national shift toward Republicans would narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arizona's 4th District leans Democratic by about four points, and incumbent Greg Stanton is seeking another term with the advantages that typically come with it. He has raised roughly $2.1 million and holds about $2.0 million on hand, while Republican Zuhdi Jasser has raised about $565,000 with $342,000 available. A Libertarian, Tisha Benoit, is also on the ballot. No outside groups have spent against Stanton, and a modest amount of outside support has backed him.

No public general-election polls are available, so expectations rest on fundamentals and market pricing. Polymarket puts Stanton's chances near 97 percent. Jasser has attracted neither significant funding nor outside backing. The combination of a district that favors the incumbent's party, a large money edge, and strong market confidence makes this a Safe Democratic seat, with the main open question being the size of the winning margin rather than the winner.
